script.text: Last month was the hottest October ever measured. What comes next?

Copernicus, the European Union's climate service, says October's global air temperature was one point seven five degrees above pre-industrial levels. That is the warmest October on record. And the third month in a row above one point five.

The oceans set a record too. Copernicus says the average sea surface temperature outside the polar regions was twenty point nine five degrees Celsius. That is the highest for any October, ahead of the old mark from twenty twenty-three.

Copernicus scientist Samantha Burgess says a very strong El Niño is adding heat to a climate already warmed by human activity. Copernicus says twenty twenty-six will most likely be the second warmest year, with a one in five chance of matching twenty twenty-four.
Will twenty twenty-seven be the hottest year on record? Yes or no?

upload.description:
Copernicus says October 2026 was the warmest October on record, 1.75°C above pre-industrial levels, and ocean surface temperatures also hit an October record of 20.95°C. Copernicus now expects 2026 to be the second warmest year.

Sources: Copernicus Climate Change Service, reported by Reuters, AFP and Down To Earth (based on search-result excerpts). Warm areas on the map are illustrative.
